chapter: Woody Herman, Condon's and Buddy Rich
title: House drummer at Eddie Condon's and the Metropolitan Bopera House
summary: He is house drummer at Condon's for three years, plays bass in after-hours sessions with famous drummers, and leads his own Sunday band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: He was a character. He used to come into Eddie Condon’s all the time, and I used to see him all the time. I mean not all the time, whenever he was in New York. Because I was the house drummer at Eddie Condon’s for three years too, which was another Dixieland club. But then on Sundays I had the Metropolitan Bopera House, my own band. And I played bass, he played drums, and some other guys would play piano after hours. I even got to play with Roy Haynes playing drums, and I’m playing bass. I got to play with some pretty good drummers at Eddie Condon’s because I played bass with that. I mean Jimmy Campbell who had been with Woody earlier on, Jackie Williams, Earl Palmer. Anybody who would come in would want to sit in and so I’d play bass and somebody else would play piano and we’d play until four in the morning. The club was open until four in the morning. Woody — all the musicians wound up hanging out there because the club was open until four. So it was like an after hours hang. We would stop playing at 1:30 or 2:00, and for two more hours the place would be open. And you never knew who © Fillius Jazz Archive -25-
was going to be coming in. Sarah Vaughan, anybody. Joe Jones would be at the end of the bar playing on a newspaper with brushes.
That guy loved to do that, didn’t he?
